title: Canadian Coins: Names, Pictures and Playing Store
seo_title: Kindergarten Canadian coins Worksheets: Free Math with Pictures and Answers (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Financial literacy: attributes and names of Canadian coins; role-playing transactions; token value
meta_desc: Free Kindergarten math worksheets on Canadian coins for the BC curriculum: nickel, dime, quarter, loonie and toonie, what is on each coin, sorting coins, trading and playing store. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: Canada has 5 coins: nickel, dime, quarter, loonie and toonie.
key_sub: A loonie is $1 and a toonie is $2. 2 loonies trade for 1 toonie.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Canada has five coins: nickel (beaver), dime (Bluenose ship), quarter (caribou), loonie (loon) and toonie (polar bear).
  • The loonie is gold with 11 sides and is worth $1. The toonie is silver with a gold middle and is worth $2.
  • The dime is the smallest coin, but it is worth more than a nickel. Size does not tell the value.
  • 2 loonies are worth the same as 1 toonie. That is a fair trade.

Examples

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Mixing up the loonie and the toonieThe loonie has the loon and 11 sides. The toonie has two colours.
Thinking the small dime is worth the leastThe dime is small, but it is worth more than a nickel.
Thinking more coins is more moneyLook at the coins, not how many. 1 toonie is more than 1 loonie.

faq.q: Which coins do Kindergarten children learn in BC?
faq.a: The nickel, dime, quarter, loonie and toonie: their names, what is on them, and their colour, size and shape.
Canada stopped making pennies in 2012. Prices are rounded, so the smallest coin used is the nickel.
A token stands for something, like a coin or a ticket you trade for a treat. Children learn that a token can be traded for something of the same value.

faq.q: How can I practise at home?
faq.a: Set up a play store with toys and price tags of $1 to $5, and pay with loonies and toonies.
